definition: Coverage is the share of dependency-bearing roots discovered in the tracked tree that are either included in a canonical clean-room SBOM, carry no declared dependencies at all, or are excluded as non-runtime under conditions re-verified on every run.
denominatorPolicy: The denominator is discovered from the tree, never hand-entered. Discovery covers declared manifests across ecosystems and components that carry third-party imports without declaring any manifest, because the second class is invisible to a manifest-only scan.
exclusionPolicy: Exclusions are computed, not listed. A component may be excluded only while every condition supporting it still holds - no container image can execute it, no root build script produces it, no deployment manifest ships it, and where applicable it is declared NOT_DEPLOYABLE in the source-controlled optional-runtime inventory. Adding a Dockerfile, build script or deployment manifest collapses the exclusion and fails the gate.
boundaries: Source dependency roots only. Built-image OS packages are not claimed.
GitHub Actions secrets and REG.RU host state are outside this metric and need their own inventory.
Remote runtime state is not claimed.
A manifest declaring no dependencies is covered because there is nothing to cover, not because an SBOM lists it.
